name: Autoclave
label: Dischord
lede: Fifteen shows, eleven songs, and two of the most distinctive songwriters DC ever produced, sharing one band for less than a year.

eras.title: Hazmat becomes a quartet
eras.text: Christina Billotte and Melissa Berkoff were a rhythm section looking for a band. Adding two guitarists, one of them Mary Timony, a college student in Boston who toured on her breaks, gave them something knotty and poppy that didn't sound like anyone else on the label.

years.h: Billotte and Berkoff start in Hazmat
years.p: [[Christina Billotte|62325e5d-014f-42a1-90d5-fa12e17aa214]], who had played in the Chrisbald 96, teams up with drummer Melissa Berkoff in a DC band called Hazmat.

years.h: [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]] and [[Nikki Chapman|c195e1c6-941b-41db-9ff3-2233f56ce93b]] join, and Hazmat becomes Autoclave
years.p: Guitarists Mary Timony and Nikki Chapman join, and Christina Billotte sings and plays bass. Bandcamp Daily later called it two generational talents in one band.
Autoclave play the Middle East club, logged by the Todestrieb archive as their Boston show, before any record is out. Mary Timony was at college in Boston and toured on her breaks.
Autoclave's first time on the road is alongside Fugazi and Beat Happening, per the band's own recollection.

years.h: Live at the Middle East, Cambridge, November 25, 1990
yt: Live at the Middle East, Cambridge, November 25, 1990

eras.title: Fifteen shows and out
eras.text: Autoclave's one 7" while they were a band was Go Far. Dischord says Autoclave defied classification and context, and it only lasted until May.

years.p: Three songs, co-released with Olympia's K Records. Bandcamp Daily heard them as caught between inspired amateurism and clever technical twists.

years.h: Autoclave split up: Olympia, New Orleans, Boston, DC
years.p: Autoclave end in May 1991. Nikki Chapman heads to Olympia, Melissa Berkoff to New Orleans, Mary Timony to Boston, and Christina Billotte stays in DC.
years.xp: Christina Billotte has described Autoclave as together off and on for two years; Dischord's dates run from summer 1990 to May 1991. Either way it was brief, and Bandcamp Daily put it neatly: they parted ways in 1991, the year punk broke.

eras.title: Helium, Slant 6, and a record after the fact
eras.text: The band was gone before most people heard it. The rest of its music came out afterward, while its two songwriters built new bands in two cities.

years.h: Autoclave's 10" EP, on Mira and Dischord
years.p: Autoclave's second and last record, released a year after the band split.

Mary Timony forms Helium; Christina Billotte forms Slant 6, later followed by [[Quix*o*tic|e4ad9a5b-7358-46be-9d34-73e9b9d072ec]] and [[The Casual Dots|d74e8159-d217-4a24-8ef0-5c2aab85a308]]. Timony has called Slant 6 one of her all-time favourite groups.

years.h: Autoclave's complete recordings on one CD · Dischord No. 108
years.p: Eleven tracks: both EPs, a song from the Simple Machines Lever 7", and live favorite Paper Boy, a cover of the Paperboy video game theme.
years.xp: Barrett Jones engineered and produced, with further recording by [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] and [[Alec Bourgeois|9de67d7e-bc5a-47fc-a00f-073d6e0519cb]]; [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] of Fugazi mixed. Maximum Rocknroll heard Christina Billotte's basslines as close to Wire, and praised her voice outright.

eras.title: A key indie text
eras.text: Autoclave never reunited. Its collected recordings kept getting pressed again anyway, and each time a new set of listeners found them.

years.p: Dischord and Mira reissue the 1997 Autoclave CD, remastered at Silver Sonya.

years.h: Autoclave's discography on vinyl at last
years.p: Autoclave's collected recordings come out as an LP. Bandcamp Daily calls it a key indie text; Pitchfork's review scores it 8.6, per Wikipedia.
